extraction.note: Answers the problem's first attack line (a native Lorentz-covariant regulator) by the extension of distributions across the coincident points, ordered by the scaling degree, the calculus of the stored Hadamard scaling results. Standard throughout: the extension theorem (Epstein and Glaser 1973, Sec. 5; Brunetti and Fredenhagen 2000, Thms. 5.2 and 5.3; imported, synthesis.imported-epstein-glaser-extension-theorem-and-ward-preserving-time-ordered-products, where the theorem numbers and statements are checked against the arXiv text); differential renormalisation and this vacuum polarisation (Freedman, Johnson and Latorre 1992; the identity Q^-2 = -(1/4) box(ln(M^2 Q)/Q) off the origin checked against eq. (1) of arXiv:hep-ph/9203207, the journal reference cited from memory); the existence of Ward-preserving time-ordered products in electrodynamics (Scharf; imported, synthesis.imported-epstein-glaser-extension-theorem-and-ward-preserving-time-ordered-products (iii)); the one-loop values (e^2/(12 pi^2), 3/(16 pi^2), Z1 = Z2) are textbook. What the store gains: the first loop result with no regulator; the vacuum polarisation coefficient, and with it the fermion weight of the running, without Pauli-Villars fields of negative weight and without the Krein-form premise (the stored one-loop result needs both); the covariant difference spaces of the one-loop extensions as exact ranks of polynomial maps in Cl(1,3) with the unit I4 (the parity-odd differences I4 and q I4 are left multiplications, distinct from the field theory's unit, which stands outside the product); the uniqueness of a vector-conserving three-current extension, which makes the axial divergence computed with Pauli-Villars fields in the triangle result (synthesis.triangle-anomaly-in-the-spacetime-algebra-is-the-pseudoscalar-part-of-the-field-square-and-cancels-per-generation) the same in every covariant vector-conserving scheme; and, as a separate step on the stored seven-dimensional commutant of the floor result, the closure and Schur argument that no smooth weighting of the floors keeps a boost. What is not proved here: that an extension obeying the Ward-Takahashi identity, transversality of the four-photon kernel, or conservation of the two vector currents exists; this is imported (Scharf; the Fact above, clause (iii)). The self-energy and vertex kernels contain the photon propagator in a covariant gauge, so the parts of clause (iii) about them are read under the Krein-form premise synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields, to which the result has an assumes edge (2 November 2026) covering those parts only; clauses (ii) and (vi) do not use it. Transport-absent for clauses (i) to (iv) and (vi); clause (v) is transport-convenient (it runs through the store's Hadamard scaling theorem) and argued; clause (vii) uses the conformal model and is transport-convenient. The Euclidean section and its continuation to the Feynman distributions are the standard Wick rotation; the unit there is the bare i of complex analysis, as the conventions allow. Clause (vii) is merged (2 November 2026) into version 3 of the floor-regulator result (synthesis.floor-regulator-keeps-the-charge-and-the-central-term-below-the-cut-off), as its clause (v).

\item[(iii)] \emph{(How Ward-preserving extensions can differ; computed.)} Among local polynomial maps in the momenta valued in $\Cl(1,3)$ (exact ranks under the six Lorentz bivector generators): the photon two-point differences of degree at most $2$ form a space of dimension $3$ ($a$, $Q(q)a$, $(a\cdot q)q$), the transverse ones dimension $1$ ($Z_{3}$); the self-energy differences of degree at most $1$ dimension $4$ ($1$, $I_{4}$, $q$, $qI_{4}$, as left multiplications), $2$ under the reflection $v \mapsto \gamma_{0}v\gamma_{0}$ ($\delta m$, $Z_{2}$); the vertex differences of degree $0$ dimension $2$ ($a$, $aI_{4}$), $1$ under the reflection; with the Ward-Takahashi identity $q_{\mu}\Lambda^{\mu} = \Sigma(p) - \Sigma(p + q)$ the joint self-energy and vertex space has dimension $2$ under the reflection ($4$ without) and forces $c_{V} = -c_{2}$, that is $Z_{1} = Z_{2}$; the three-current differences of degree at most $1$ form a space of dimension $8$, of which none is transverse on any two legs; the four-photon differences a space of dimension $4$, none transverse on one leg. The self-energy and vertex kernels contain the photon propagator in a covariant gauge, so these parts are read under the Krein-form premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}. In particular at most one covariant three-current extension (one axial, two vector legs) conserves both vector currents, so every such extension has the same axial divergence.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Status of the units.)} The parity-odd differences $I_{4}$ and $qI_{4}$ of (iii) are left multiplications; the field theory's unit stands outside the product (the conventions' right unit), so they are pseudoscalar terms removed by the reflection, not complex rescalings of $\delta m$ and $Z_{2}$, which reality of the coefficients removes.
\item[(v)] \emph{(On a gravitational field; argued.)} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-dirac-states-scale-to-the-flat-massless-vacuum-at-every-point-of-a-gravitational-field} every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field has, at every point, scaling degree $3$ with the flat massless kernel as limit; with the scaling-degree bound for products of Hadamard parametrices (Brunetti and Fredenhagen) the one-loop kernels on a gravitational field have the flat degrees of divergence and the flat leading scale coefficients, the further ambiguities being local terms in the field strength of matching dimension (Hollands and Wald \cite{HollandsWald2001}).
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Separately, the scalar field: the quartic bubble; computed.)} For a free scalar field, $\Delta_{0}^{2} = 1/(16\pi^{4}s^{2})$ extends to $- rac{1}{64\pi^{4}}
abla^{2}(L_{\mu}/s)$ with $\mu\,\partial_{\mu}$ of it equal to $\delta/(8\pi^{2})$; for $\lambda\phi^{4}/4!$ the three channels with symmetry factor $ rac12$ give $\mu\,d\lambda/d\mu = 3\lambda^{2}/(16\pi^{2})$ at one loop (standard).
\item[(vii)] \emph{(Merged.)} The separate statement once recorded here, that no smooth weighting of the floors keeps a boost, is clause (v) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.floor-regulator-keeps-the-charge-and-the-central-term-below-the-cut-off}, into which it was merged on 2 November 2026; it is stated and proved there, and this result no longer states it.
\end{enumerate}
levels.technical:
The stored one-loop electrodynamics uses Pauli-Villars fields, some of negative weight, so its regulator rests on the same indefinite form as the covariant gauge; the floors of the tower keep the Ward identity but no boost. A standard alternative (Epstein and Glaser; in this computational form, Freedman, Johnson and Latorre) needs no regulator: the one-loop kernels are well defined away from coincident points, and extending them across is the only step that needs a choice, governed by the scaling degree, the calculus of the stored Hadamard scaling results. Carried out in the spacetime algebra on the Euclidean section, the vacuum polarisation away from the origin, including the order-$m^{2}$ term from the Klein-Gordon recursion, is $(e^{2}/(12\pi^{4}))T(s^{-2})$ minus $(e^{2}m^{2}/(8\pi^{4}))T(s^{-1})$ plus a part of low scaling degree, $T$ the transverse operator $a \mapsto (a\cdot
abla)
abla - a
abla^{2}$. Writing $s^{-2}$ as a Laplacian of the locally integrable $\ln(\mu^{2}s)/s$ gives an extension that is transverse and covariant by construction; its dependence on the scale $\mu$ is a multiple of $T(\delta)$, whose coefficient $e^{2}/(6\pi^{2})$ is twice the magnitude $e^{2}/(12\pi^{2})$ of the stored log coefficient. No regulator field and no photon line, so no Krein form, enters. For the other one-loop kernels the result is narrower: exact rank computations in $\Cl(1,3)$ show how covariant extensions obeying the Ward identities and the reflection can differ (exactly by $Z_{3}$, $\delta m$ and $Z_{2} = Z_{1}$, not at all for the three- and four-photon kernels, and at most one vector-conserving three-current extension, so one axial divergence), while their existence is the imported part (Scharf's Ward-preserving time-ordered products); the self-energy and vertex kernels carry the covariant photon propagator and so hold under the Krein-form premise. On a gravitational field the Hadamard scaling theorem gives every Dirac two-point function the flat scaling degree, so the same counting carries over with terms in the field strength added (argued). A separate statement is recorded with it: the scalar bubble gives the standard quartic coefficient $3/(16\pi^{2})$. The statement that no smooth weighting of the floors keeps a boost, once a clause here, is now clause (v) of the floor-regulator result.
levels.lay: Calculations with quantum loops produce infinities that are usually tamed by a regulator, an artificial modification at very high energies removed at the end. The series had used borrowed regulators, one of which needs fictitious particles with negative probabilities, and its own natural cut-off, the floors of its tower, singles out one observer and so breaks relativity. A known method, extending the loop quantities across the points where they are singular, is here carried out in the series' algebra. For the screening of electric charge by the vacuum it needs no regulator and no fictitious particles, stays relativistic, keeps charge conservation, and gives the standard strength of screening. For the other one-loop quantities the calculation shows that the only freedom left by relativity and charge conservation is the three constants physicists already adjust (the electron's mass, the normalisation of its field and the strength of the charge); that a version keeping charge conservation exists there is taken from the literature, and for the electron's own corrections the photon's states are assumed to carry the standard indefinite measure of the series' premise. The whole calculation assumes the standard theorem on extending such quantities, also taken from the literature. A related statement, that no smoothing of the tower's floors can restore relativity, is recorded with the result on the floors.
levels.one-liner: Standard (Epstein and Glaser 1973; Freedman, Johnson and Latorre 1992), now in the store: under the imported extension theorem the one-loop vacuum polarisation in the spacetime algebra extends with no regulator to a covariant transverse kernel with log coefficient of magnitude $e^{2}/(12\pi^{2})$ per Dirac fermion, using no Pauli-Villars field and no Krein form; Ward-preserving covariant extensions of the other one-loop kernels, if they exist (imported, not proved; self-energy and vertex under the Krein-form premise), differ only by $Z_{3}$, $\delta m$, $Z_{2} = Z_{1}$, and the vector-conserving three-current extension is unique, so its axial divergence is scheme independent; separately, the scalar bubble gives $3/(16\pi^{2})$ (the floors' weighting statement is now the floor-regulator result's clause (v)); transport-absent except clause (v), transport-convenient.
